title: Individual enforcement resolutions can document paid remedy while leaving durable recovery open
source_unit: US Department of Justice Immigrant and Employee Rights Section FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary
geography: United States; named charging-party employment and recruitment discrimination resolutions

observations.period: December 11, 2025 IER resolution; summary updated September 15, 2026

denominator.unit: named charging-party resolution summarized by IER

reported_exposure.value: A naturalized US citizen alleged a staffing company withdrew a position after requesting citizenship proof

individual_remedy.unit: US dollars in back pay; IER summary states the charging party received it

institutional_response.value: Relevant staff training on the anti-discrimination provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act

observations.method: Targeted review of the official IER FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary; the page's agency-reported payment and control action are kept separate from later worker outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not identify the company or worker, provide a payment instrument or date, or report continued employment, comparable opportunity, household recovery, trust, or later action.
observations.subgroup: One naturalized US citizen charging party in the IER summary; no population denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A reported payment can address assessed back pay without recreating the lost opportunity or establishing durable correction.

observations.period: February 20, 2026 IER resolution; summary updated September 15, 2026

denominator.unit: named charging-party resolution summarized by IER

reported_exposure.value: A building-supply-chain worker alleged retaliation and unfair documentary practice after termination of a lawful permanent resident

individual_remedy.unit: US dollars paid to the charging party; IER found no reasonable cause for a violation but identified practice deficiencies

observations.method: Targeted review of the official IER FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary; payment, finding status, and training are coded as distinct stages.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not identify the company or worker, provide payment timing or receipt documentation beyond the agency statement, or report reinstatement, later employment, household recovery, trust, or action.
observations.subgroup: One charging party in the IER summary; no population denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: Payment and training can resolve a documented administrative deficiency without proving discrimination, durable compliance, or restored employment.

observations.period: May 28, 2026 IER resolution; summary updated September 15, 2026

denominator.unit: named charging-party resolution summarized by IER

reported_exposure.value: A worker alleged termination discrimination and unfair documentary practice involving an asylum I-94 during reverification

individual_remedy.unit: US dollars in back pay; IER summary states the charging party was paid

observations.method: Targeted review of the official IER FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary; paid back pay, reinstatement offer, and training are not merged into a completed return-to-work outcome.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not report whether reinstatement was accepted, whether work resumed, payment timing or instrument, continued employment, household recovery, trust, or later action.
observations.subgroup: One charging party in the IER summary; no population denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A paid remedy plus an offer of reinstatement creates a stronger response route than a prospective fund, but an offer is not accepted reemployment or durable recovery.

observations.period: June 17, 2026 IER resolution; summary updated September 15, 2026

denominator.unit: named charging-party resolution summarized by IER

reported_exposure.value: A US citizen alleged termination after an E-Verify tentative nonconfirmation and employer refusal to rerun the case using the Social Security Administration's instructed name format

individual_remedy.unit: US dollars in front pay and back pay; IER summary states the employee received it

institutional_response.value: Form I-9 and E-Verify policies were created and human-resources employees were trained

observations.method: Targeted review of the official IER FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary; front pay, back pay, policy change, and training are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not report payment timing or receipt documentation beyond the agency statement, reinstatement, later employment, household recovery, trust, or action.
observations.subgroup: One charging party in the IER summary; no population denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: Front and back pay can compensate a terminated worker without restoring the original job or demonstrating durable institutional change.

observations.period: September 4, 2026 IER resolution; summary updated September 15, 2026

denominator.unit: named charging-party resolution summarized by IER

reported_exposure.value: A transferred worker alleged forced resignation and non-hire after becoming a lawful permanent resident

individual_remedy_offer.unit: US dollars in full back pay and benefits offered; payment is not reported

institutional_response.value: The company changed policy to explicitly prohibit citizenship-status discrimination

observations.method: Targeted review of the official IER FY2026 letters-of-resolution summary; the offer is deliberately separated from paid-remedy cases.
observations.uncertainty: The summary does not report acceptance or payment, reinstatement, later employment, household recovery, trust, or action.
observations.subgroup: One charging party in the IER summary; no population denominator.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large back-pay offer indicates a potentially material remedy route but cannot be coded as payment, restored opportunity, or recovery.

related_sources.claim: The IER case ledger supplies the broader federal worker-protection enforcement context.
The worker/workplace ledger specifies the missing post-remedy work, household, voice, and exit fields.

boundary: This record adds five official IER resolution summaries, including four agency-reported individual paid-remedy cases and one back-pay offer. It strengthens the verified-remedy stage at case level but does not establish payment receipt independently, restored opportunity, continued work, household recovery, trust, political action, switching, or exit; the cases are not pooled into a prevalence estimate.
